title: NVIDIA MMS1X00-N5400 QSFP112 1310NM 400Gbps Optic Quick Look
gist: A hands-on look at NVIDIA's MMS1X00-N5400 QSFP112 1310nm 400Gbps optic, bought to link GB300 AI Station systems to a Spectrum-X switch via ConnectX-8 NICs; the module's 4x112G PAM4 design avoids the gearbox that QSFP56-DD parts need, draws a maximum of 10W, and ran in the mid-40C range.

insights.claim: A QSFP112 optic delivers 400Gbps over four 112G PAM4 lanes, while cheaper QSFP56-DD parts need eight 56G PAM4 lanes and therefore a physically different connector, making the two ecosystems non-interchangeable at the port.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Lane-rate generation, not headline port speed, determines which optics and switches a buyer is locked into — a cost split worth tracking in optics suppliers' mix.
insights.quote: As a result, QSFP56-DD is a different connector from QSFP112 because it needs eight channels instead of four back to the device.
insights.locator: The connector here is important since

insights.claim: Native 112G-lane optics remove the need for an in-module gearbox when connecting a 400Gbps 500m DR4 link, simplifying the bill of materials versus a QSFP56-DD path.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Gearbox elimination is a quiet cost and power lever as 400G/800G optics volumes scale.
insights.quote: the advantage here is that, unlike using a QSFP56-DD module, we do not need a gearbox in the module to connect a 400Gbps 500m DR4 link from our switch
insights.locator: We tend to run a lot of DR4/ LR4 optics

insights.claim: QSFP112 is a more compact pluggable form factor than the OSFP packaging that dominates at 800Gbps and 1.6Tbps, giving 400G ports a density advantage at the low end of AI networking.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Form-factor fragmentation across 400G/800G/1.6T means connector and cage suppliers see multiple concurrent product cycles.
insights.locator: That means we get a standard pluggable form factor

insights.claim: The module uses an MPO-12 connector but lights only eight of the twelve fibers because it is a 4x112G design, meaning installed 12-fiber MPO/MTP singlemode plant is already future-headroomed for these links.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Existing 12-fiber structured cabling does not need replacing for this generation, dampening near-term fiber-plant capex.

themes.theme: Thermal design in liquid-cooled AI racks

insights.claim: NVIDIA attaches small external heatsinks to these 400Gbps modules that protrude from the NIC and switch, rather than relying on cooling built into the device's pluggable cages as is typical at 400Gbps.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Optics thermal management is migrating into the module itself — a design cost that favors vendor-branded optics over generics.
insights.quote: Here though, NVIDIA is using a small heatsink on the outside of the device so they stick out a bit from the NIC and switch.
insights.locator: Something else neat is that NVIDIA adds small heatsinks

insights.claim: The optic reports a 10W maximum power draw and ran in the mid-40C range in a live system, well below its thermal threshold.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Per-port optical power near 10W at 400G sets the per-rack optics power budget that datacenter designers must provision for.
insights.quote: We can see here that it is reporting as a 10W maximum device.

insights.claim: Liquid-cooled GB300 AI Station machines provide little active cooling for optical modules, which is a stated reason to buy NVIDIA-branded optics that tolerate higher hot-aisle temperatures better than popular generic modules in large AI clusters.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Liquid cooling shifts the thermal burden onto optics and creates a durable premium-pricing moat for first-party NVIDIA transceivers over third-party alternatives.
insights.quote: in large AI clusters, NVIDIA optics tend to run well at higher temperatures on the hot-aisle side than some popular generic modules

insights.claim: These optics cost more than a DAC cable but were judged worth it for switch-swapping flexibility and for direct GB300-to-GB300 links over 12-fiber MPO/MTP singlemode cable using ConnectX-8 NICs.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Optics-versus-DAC substitution at 400G turns on flexibility and reach, not just unit price — relevant to copper-cable versus transceiver volume forecasts.

insights.claim: The 400GbE link autonegotiated almost instantaneously on the ConnectX-8 NIC inside a GB300 AI Station, indicating first-party NVIDIA optic, NIC and Spectrum-X switch combinations require no tuning.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Frictionless first-party interop is the practical mechanism behind NVIDIA's networking attach rate.
insights.quote: This autonegotiated almost instantaneously on the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 NIC that is part of that platform.
